method: Exp 1: 30 containers, 2-yr seedlings of black oak and red maple vs no tree, clay loam compacted to 1.31 or 1.59 g/cm3, saturated, 1 L infiltration test on 6 dates (May-Sept 2006). Exp 2: green ash (n=5) vs no tree (n=5) in 78:22 stone:soil structural soil over compacted clay loam (1.63 g/cm3) behind a woven geotextile, constant-head Ksat after 2 yr
traits_or_metrics: Infiltration rate (mL/s), saturated hydraulic conductivity Ksat (cm/s), root counts
key_quantified_results: Trees raised infiltration by 63% on average (all treatments pooled) and 153% in the more compacted soil; approximate Ksat at 1.59 g/cm3: 1.3e-3 (no tree), 3.0e-3 (red maple), 3.9e-3 (black oak) cm/s, i.e. ~47, 108, 140 mm/h. Exp 2: Ksat 1.31e-3 vs 4.83e-5 cm/s with vs without green ash (27x; ~47 vs ~1.7 mm/h), P=0.008, 6.3 roots per tree through the geotextile. Black oak (coarse roots) vs red maple (fine roots): not significantly different (P 0.1-0.9 across dates). Structural soil: ~20% mineral soil, 30-35% porosity once compacted; growth-limiting dry density for clay loam 1.45-1.55 g/cm3
limits_noted: Containers, young trees (green ash 1.8 m after 2 yr), irrigated and repeatedly saturated (soil strength low, flood-tolerant species), free-draining pots, infiltration fell 53% on average across all treatments over the season (the authors suggest settling); Ksat is a relative lab value for the most restrictive layer, not a field pit rate; Platanus x acerifolia is suggested by the authors as a suitable species but was not tested
relevance_to_topic: Roots do raise infiltration through compacted subsoil, but the root-architecture (species) effect is NOT shown: keeps roots out of the species scoring. citation: Esposito, Pappaccogli, Donateo et al. 2024 (Remote Sens. 16:4496)
file_in_papers: Urban Morphology and Surface Urban Heat Island Relationship During Heat Waves A Study of Milan and Lecce (Italy).pdf
method: Sentinel-3 LST (1 km, day and night), JJA/DJF 2022-2023, vs morphology (building height, SVF, aspect ratio, building and impervious fractions); heatwaves by WSDI; multiple regression
traits_or_metrics: Surface UHI intensity (SUHII)
key_quantified_results: Summer SUHII: Milan 4.25 C day / 1.92 C night; Lecce -1.08 C day (surface cool island, dry rural soils) / 0.72 C night; heatwave nights slightly higher (Milan +0.35 C) but not significant; night SUHII rises with impervious fraction in both cities
limits_noted: 1 km surface temperature, two summers
relevance_to_topic: Daytime satellite surface UHI can invert in a dry Mediterranean summer -> poor proxy for pedestrian heat; supports UTCI/MRT at street level

citation: Campanale, Adinolfi, Raffa, Schulz & Mercogliano 2025 (Urban Clim. 60:102335)
file_in_papers: Investigating urban heat islands over Rome and Milan during a summer period through the TERRA_URB parameterization in the ICON model.pdf

traits_or_metrics: 2 m air temperature, UHI intensity, heat fluxes

citation: Petralli, Prokopp, Morabito, Bartolini, Torrigiani & Orlandini 2006 (Riv. Ital. Agrometeorol. 2006(1):51-58)
file_in_papers: RUOLO DELLE AREE VERDI NELLA MITIGAZIONE DELL’ISOLA DI CALORE.pdf
method: 18 air-temperature loggers at ~2 m in streets, courtyards (< 500 m2) and gardens across 4 concentric zones of building density; May 2005, clear calm days
traits_or_metrics: Air temperature, Park Cool Island (street - green area)
key_quantified_results: Park Cool Island street - garden: 1.44 C (centre I), 1.40 C (centre II), 0.76 C (first periphery, F I); street - courtyard < 0.5 C; central evenings: difference grows from ~1 C before sunset to ~2 C at 23:00; before dawn gardens ~1.5 C cooler than streets

file_in_papers: Grey 2018 - Tree pits to help mitigate runoff in dense urban areas.pdf
method: 15 kerb-inlet tree pits (0.72 m2, 100 mm detention; native clay, biofilter sand, or tree beside the pit) with young Acer campestre, monitored Sep 2015-Dec 2016; per-pit water-balance model calibrated and validated, then applied to street-scale scenarios
traits_or_metrics: Runoff retention (%), runoff days per year, exfiltration rate, pit-to-catchment area ratio
key_quantified_results: Pits = 0.3% of their catchment (median 200 m2): median total retention 11% (4-33%), no difference among designs; model NSE 0.71 calibration / 0.69 validation; median exfiltration 6 mm/h (1-34); exfiltration removes >= 88% of the water, tree ET ~4% (young trees); scenarios: as built 5%, avenue planting 26%, avenue on public realm only 49%; ~90% retention and 15 runoff days/yr need pits of 2.5-8% of their impervious catchment (4.4% at 6 mm/h)
limits_noted: One street, heavy clay, young trees, one year modelled; fate of exfiltrated water unknown (authors)
relevance_to_topic: Pit-to-catchment ratio and native-soil exfiltration decide pit retention; the measured pits (0.3% of their catchment) kept a median 11%, and 5% in the modelled whole-catchment case with roofs. Numbers for backup slide B1 and a pit module

citation: Thom, Szota, Coutts, Fletcher & Livesley 2020 (Water Res. 173:115597)
file_in_papers: Thom 2020 - Transpiration by established trees could increase the efficiency of stormwater control measures.pdf
method: 9 established Lophostemon confertus street trees (evergreen; canopy ~13-16 m2): 3 controls, 6 with a 6 m2 unlined infiltration trench (2.4-4.6% of a ~200 m2 impervious catchment); sap flow Oct-Mar 2014-2016, soil moisture, trench water level; annual water balance for 2015
traits_or_metrics: Transpiration per canopy area, stormwater retention, water balance
key_quantified_results: Transpiration 0.7-6.2 mm/d per canopy area (10.8-96.1 L/d), mean 3.5 mm/d, not higher next to trenches (p = 0.86; trees not water-limited); event retention 30%; annual retention 24% of runoff and tree transpiration = 17% of runoff; 76% of runoff bypassed (inlet design, clogging)
limits_noted: One species (evergreen), one street, year-round rain; transpiration predicted from ETo for Apr-Sep (authors)
relevance_to_topic: Established crowns can transpire the equivalent of a large share of their catchment's runoff, so the canopy-to-catchment ratio is a design variable; but the trenches did not raise transpiration. Deciduous trees would transpire little in winter (authors, citing Harper et al. 2015); in Barcelona most intense storms fall in Sep-Oct (storm_months.csv), so leaf-off matters mainly for Nov-Jan rain

citation: Thom, Livesley, Fletcher, Farrell, Arndt, Konarska & Szota 2022 (Sci. Total Environ. 812:151466; online 2021)
file_in_papers: Thom 2022 - Selecting tree species with high transpiration and drought avoidance to optimise runoff reduction.pdf
method: 13 street-tree species, young potted trees (70 L) on scales under a rain shelter: well-watered, water deficit, rewatering (Feb-Apr 2019); crop factor, hydroscape area, transpiration recovery; relation to turgor loss point, Huber value, wood density
traits_or_metrics: Crop factor KC, hydroscape area, transpiration recovery, Huber value
key_quantified_results: KC 0.33-1.56; high (> 1.15): Lophostemon confertus, Callistemon viminalis, Pyrus calleryana, Tristaniopsis laurina; low (< 0.75): Agonis flexuosa, Eucalyptus pauciflora, Acer campestre, Corymbia ficifolia; hydroscape 1.4-5.1 MPa2; recovery 35-109%; only T. laurina high on all three; Huber value related to KC (R2 0.25) and recovery (R2 0.51)
limits_noted: Young potted trees; crop factors change with life stage; no field test (authors)
relevance_to_topic: Species angle for pits: Pyrus calleryana (palette) has a high crop factor; cites Jacaranda mimosifolia at 9 L/d vs Lagerstroemia indica 45 L/d (Pataki et al. 2011, Los Angeles)

file_in_papers: Tan 2026 - Surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization of micro-scale urban tree configurations.pdf
method: Rhino/Grasshopper + GhPython: radiation (Honeybee + CityComfort+, species-specific Beer-Lambert canopy transmittance) + OpenFOAM CFD (trees as porous media with LAD-weighted heat and vapour sources) -> UTCI; Random Forest surrogate on 1,500 simulations; NSGA-II (60 x 50) places 30 trees of 4 species on 108 candidate locations of a 45 x 60 m block; Pareto solutions re-simulated
traits_or_metrics: Site-mean, min and max UTCI; Shannon species diversity; 20-yr CO2 uptake; species LAI and crown size from US allometry (5-yr-old trees)
key_quantified_results: Surrogate RMSE 0.09 C (site-mean UTCI), Kendall tau 0.84; ~5 min per optimisation run; no-tree site-mean UTCI 39.07 C -> 37.71 C best (-1.36 C), share of site above 38 C 95% -> 55%; a balanced solution trades 0.55 C for +25% CO2 uptake and ~3x diversity; configurations differ by 0.55-1.32 C site-mean
limits_noted: No site-specific field validation, partial radiation-CFD coupling, one peak hour, US allometry, micro-scale only (authors)
relevance_to_topic: Closest precedent: optimises species and positions of a fixed 30 trees with species-resolved crowns and co-benefits, with a similar Grasshopper + NSGA-II approach and a Random Forest surrogate (this thesis: pre-computed shade x tau proxy, NSGA-II planned); heat only, no runoff -> the gap narrows to heat and runoff together

citation: Santos Nouri, Frohlich, Matos Silva & Matzarakis 2018 (Atmosphere 9:12)
file_in_papers: Santos Nouri 2018 - The Impact of Tipuana tipu Species on Local Human Thermal Comfort Thresholds.pdf
method: SkyHelios (sky view, diagnostic wind) + RayMan (PET, mPET) for symmetric street canyons 20 m high and 10-120 m wide (H/W 2.0-0.17), NS and WE, with and without Tipuana tipu (12.5 m tall, crown 10-13 m wide); crown transmissivity from global radiation measured under crowns; 3 Jul and 16 Dec 2016
traits_or_metrics: PET, mPET, Tmrt at reference points
key_quantified_results: Summer: PET up to -15.6 C (mPET -11.6 C) under the tree (H/W 0.17, WE, 16:00); Tmrt -13.1 to -29.5 C across canyons. Winter: Tipuana keeps its leaves (leafless only in early spring in Iberia, as cited), PET up to -2.7 C (mPET -2.6 C) at noon, i.e. overshading
limits_noted: Model estimates (wind from a diagnostic model), single trees, no field validation of PET (authors)
relevance_to_topic: First-hand (modelled) cooling value for a palette species, and a winter case that assumes Tipuana stays leafed (phenology cited from Vinas & Solanich, not observed): consistent with the tool's base case; the Porta field check is still needed

citation: Ji et al. 2025 (Urban For. Urban Green. 113:129068)
file_in_papers: (not in papers/)
method: Field: canopy interception, throughfall, stemflow of Cinnamomum camphora, Sophora japonica (= Styphnolobium) and Platanus orientalis over 20 rainfall events, 2022-2023; effects of rainfall, canopy structure, meteorology and leaf micro-traits
traits_or_metrics: Interception per event, throughfall, stemflow; plant size, biomass, leaf wettability and microstructure
key_quantified_results: Throughfall 17.3-17.6 mm, canopy interception 4.0-4.3 mm, stemflow 0.06-0.1 mm per event (averages for the three species); rainfall amount linear and dominant; interception and throughfall largely independent of canopy structure and other meteorological variables; storage capacity depends on size, biomass, wettability and microstructure but this is attenuated under natural rain
limits_noted: (abs) Three species, one city, 20 events; abstract only; per-species numbers not read
relevance_to_topic: Qualifies the topic_decision section 1 traits-vs-biomass row and the H1 mechanism: under natural rain, event rainfall amount outweighed canopy and leaf traits, so trait effects on runoff should be tested at design-storm scale, not assumed from storage capacity
